A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same ProcessBench study with readable main text, mathematical definitions, seven figures, nine tables, and complete appendices. The added inference appendix and subsequent appendix renumbering can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-annotation analyses and model evaluations on 3,400 ProcessBench cases, including the authors' trained PRM and appendix threshold and greedy-decoding evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark analyses and experimental results in Tables 2–3 and 5–9 and Figures 3–5.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction procedures, PRM reward head and classification loss, and critic prompt remain unchanged. The new inference appendix supplies implementation details without reporting a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH, OlympiadBench, and Omni-MATH for the same 3,400-case earliest-error benchmark and PRM800K for training. Dataset, generator, and task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 5–9 retain the same Math-Shepherd, RLHFlow, Skywork, authors' PRM, and critic-model comparisons. The added Luo et al. citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Previously stated sample counts, filtering procedures, accuracy/F1 metrics, threshold selection, and voting versus greedy-decoding protocols remain unchanged. Appendix D newly discloses sampling parameters for existing experiments; it does not report a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The error-position and per-generator process-error analyses, QwQ critique example, Skywork threshold checks, and greedy-decoding comparisons are retained unchanged (Figures 3–5; Tables 6, 8–9). No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-variability estimates. Annotation-agreement reporting and eight-sample voting are unchanged; the latter remains an inference aggregation procedure.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, dataset statistics, and qualitative examples remain unchanged, including all appendix results. For example, Table 3 retains average F1 scores of 56.5 for Qwen2.5-Math-7B-PRM800K and 71.5 for QwQ-32B-Preview.

T1.justification: The formal earliest-error task and error definitions in Section 3.1 are unchanged, as are the metric definition and training objective. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or substantive derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the benchmark contribution and headline claims: existing PRMs generalize poorly, and QwQ is competitive with GPT-4o while trailing o1-mini. No core contribution or claim is redefined.

C2.justification: v1 already reports roughly 30% annotation discards and warns about inaccurate labels. v3 additionally acknowledges that discarded solutions may involve particularly difficult problems, potentially biasing the benchmark's problem distribution (Section 5).

D1.justification: Appendices C–D add training/inference hardware details (eight A100 80GB GPUs), the vLLM backend, and generation and voting sampling parameters, including special settings for Qwen2.5-Math. The title page adds a direct Hugging Face dataset link alongside the existing GitHub link.

R1.justification: v3 adds Luo et al. (2024) on automated process supervision and Kwon et al. (2023) for vLLM. Related work more explicitly distinguishes specialized PRMs from general language models, while the benchmark's research positioning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited spelling and grammar edits, author and corresponding-author updates, and renaming of Section 3.2 to Data Collection. A new Inference Details appendix shifts subsequent appendix labels; the overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: The added title-page link and appendix text shift Figures 1 and 7 vertically, with other small placement changes from text reflow. All seven figures and nine tables retain their content, captions, and display designs.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility through explicit sampling settings, backend and hardware details, and direct dataset access information. Its new selection-bias caveat also improves transparency about the existing annotation filter. These address limited documentation and interpretation gaps while leaving the empirical evidence unchanged.
